answer.summary: Migrated wolverine from openai v1 globals to explicit v2 clients. Removed the import-time openai.api_key assignment and added a lazy _get_client() factory returning openai.OpenAI(api_key=...), so importing wolverine still works with OPENAI_API_KEY unset and a missing key only fails when an API call is attempted. Switched openai.ChatCompletion.create() to client.chat.completions.create() and openai.Model.list()["data"] dict access to client.models.list().data attribute access with m.id. Existing attribute-style response access (response.choices[0].message.content) and the verbatim message append already match the pydantic model shape, verified end-to-end against a real ChatCompletion object over a mocked transport. Pinned openai<2,>=1 in requirements.txt, updated the test mock target literal to openai.resources.chat.completions.Completions.create, and added an autouse fixture supplying a dummy key since v2 clients require one at construction (no network is touched). All 6 tests pass and the --revert path runs without a key.

findings.explanation: DriftSpec type_changes requires responses are pydantic models requiring attribute access (completion.choices[0].text, model.model_dump()). Diff migrates the create call but shows no migration of downstream response handling. If json_validated_response still uses dict subscript (response['choices'][0]['message']['content']) it will fail on real v2 responses even if tests pass with a dict-compatible MagicMock.
findings.suggested_fix: Audit json_validated_response and any other response consumers to use attribute access (response.choices[0].message.content) and model_dump()/model_dump_json() where dict conversion is needed.

findings.explanation: Helper constructs a new OpenAI client on every API call instead of reusing a singleton. Correct per spec but silently changes connection pooling, cleanup and auto-retry state vs a persistent client instance.
findings.suggested_fix: Cache the client lazily at module level (or allow injection) and reuse it rather than instantiating on each call.

findings.explanation: Uses .data attribute which returns only first page, not the automatic iteration the spec promotes to replace auto_paging_iter(). Functionally equivalent to old single-page behavior but will miss models beyond first page if pagination matters.
findings.suggested_fix: Consider iterating directly over client.models.list() (automatic pagination) or document that only first page is checked.
